notes: Circuit: a two-mesh-plus network. Reading the drawing before any machine output: top rail runs from the top-left corner (270,375) right through the 2H inductor #1, past the node where the 9F capacitor #2 hangs down (437,350), into the 3V source #0 (circle with + on the left, - on the right), then to the top-right corner (622,343) and down the right-hand rail. A horizontal wire at y~480 runs from that rail right to the GND symbol #5 and left to the right plate of the 5F capacitor #4; the 3H inductor #6 hangs down from it. A middle horizontal rail at y~505 runs from the bottom of the 4Omega resistor #3 (285,510) right, past the bottom lead of the 9F cap and the top of the 6Omega resistor #7, to the left plate of the 5F cap. The 2A current source #8 hangs below (285,510) down to the bottom rail, which runs right to the bottom of 6Omega and the bottom of 3H. NET MAP (5 nets, 9 components): n2 = top-left corner - left lead of inductor 2H #1 and top lead of resistor 4Omega #3. n1 = right lead of 2H #1, top plate of the 9F capacitor #2, and the left (+) terminal of the 3V source #0. 0 = the right (-) terminal of the 3V source #0, the top-right corner, the whole right-hand rail down to y~480, the horizontal run east to the GND symbol #5, the right plate of the 5F capacitor #4 and the top lead of the 3H inductor #6. n3 = the middle rail at y~505: bottom lead of 4Omega #3, top terminal of the 2A source #8, bottom lead of the 9F capacitor #2, top lead of the 6Omega resistor #7 and the left plate of the 5F capacitor #4. n4 = the bottom rail: bottom terminal of the 2A source #8, bottom lead of 6Omega #7 and bottom lead of 3H #6. SITE DECISIONS (all six CRITICAL sites inspected in the crops, and S13 additionally in the raw pixels): S3 (432,359) JUNCTION - clean T, the 9F top lead rises and terminates on the top rail; the alternative would strand the capacitor's top plate on a one-terminal net. S11 (627,479) JUNCTION - the vertical right-hand rail comes down from the top-right corner and ends on the y~480 horizontal (nothing continues below at that x); reading it as anything else would leave the 3V source's return with no path to GND. S12 (611,484) JUNCTION - the 3H inductor's top lead rises and ends on the same y~480 horizontal, a clean T 16 px west of S11; not joining it would leave the inductor's top terminal dangling. S13 (449,501) JUNCTION - this is the one real judgement call on the sheet. It is a plain X: a single smooth stroke descends from the 9F capacitor's bottom lead (x~441 at y=475, x~447 at y=500, x~455 at y=527) straight into the top of the 6Omega resistor, and the middle rail crosses it as one smooth slightly-descending stroke (y~504 at x=423 to y~496 at x=475). inkmap at (449,501) win=26 shows no solder blob (dot metric 1.5, i.e. ~1.5x stroke width, nowhere near the ~3x a real dot gives), no semicircular hop, and only a 2-3 px lateral offset of the vertical across the crossing, which is ordinary hand tremor rather than a deliberate jog (the reported hop=4.2 is that same small offset). Both readings are electrically sane - the crossing reading would give a 2-terminal net {9F bottom, 6Omega top} and a 3-terminal net {4Omega bottom, 2A top, 5F left}, with no islands and no shorted source - so rule 1 does not settle it and the dataset ink prior applies: a bare crossing with neither dot nor hop is a junction. The drafter used no hops or jogs anywhere on this sheet, so there is no counter-habit to appeal to. Consequence of the other reading: the middle rail would split in two, giving 6 nets instead of 5, the 9F capacitor would sit in series with the 6Omega resistor between the top node and the bottom rail, and the 5F capacitor would connect to the 4Omega/2A node instead of to the 9F/6Omega column. S14 (291,519) JUNCTION - the left column runs continuously from the bottom of 4Omega down into the 2A source and the middle rail branches east from it; a plain T, and not joining it would leave the middle rail with no connection to the left branch. S16 (482,641) JUNCTION - the 6Omega bottom lead descends and terminates on the bottom rail; not joining it would strand the resistor's bottom terminal. NON-CRITICAL SITES left at their defaults: S0/S1/S2 (the handwritten '2H' label brushing the inductor box), S5/S6/S7/S8 ('5F'), S9/S10 ('4Omega'), S15 ('3H'). All 11 gap bridges are inside those same label blobs and none changes the netlist. PORTS: every component's terminals already sit on the real leads - checked each in the comps montage. The unused port candidates flagged in the warnings (V-DC at 551,312 and 563,314; 9F cap at 395,430 and 394,407; 5F cap at 536,455 and 557,452; 6Omega at 484,577 / 489,545 / 484,560) are all strokes of the handwritten value labels ('3V', '9F', '5F', '6Omega') that touch the annotated boxes, not leads, so no port remapping was needed. CLASSES: all nine as labelled - coil = Inductor (2H, 3H), zig-zag = Resistor (4Omega, 6Omega), parallel plates = Capacitor (9F, 5F), circle with +/- = V-DC (3V), circle with a bare arrow = I-DC (2A), three bars = GND. Nothing left unresolved.
